turns.question: What is the retention outcome for uploads that may still be referenced by completed reports: hard-delete the original object after a defined interval from report completion, or retain indefinitely once any completed report references it? Recommended: hard-delete uploads 90 days after the last referencing report reaches terminal state, while preserving non-file report summaries.

What recovery semantic should govern user-facing deletion given disaster-recovery backups retain objects for 30 days: should the product promise reversible deletion during backup retention, or state deletion as final at the application layer? Recommended: declare deletion final to users and treat backup copies as operator-only disaster recovery, not customer-restorable state.

contract.G: Define a defensible retention policy for customer uploads without breaking completed report records.
contract.T: Specify lifecycle rules for uploaded objects, derived report artifacts, and user-facing deletion semantics.
contract.S: Production uploads referenced by reports, retained report summaries, scheduled cleanup, and backup interaction; excludes redesign of backup systems.
contract.V: Confirm uploads are deleted 90 days after the last report finishes, report summaries remain accessible, cleanup skips active references, and user-facing copy states deletion is final despite 30-day DR backup aging.
contract.X: Stop if legal/compliance retention requirements appear, if reports require original uploads for replay beyond 90 days, or if backup restore is intended as a user recovery feature.
contract.P: Persist with guided policy definition only; do not implement cleanup jobs or storage changes.

promotions.name: Last Referencing Report Finish
promotions.evidence: Retention trigger depends on the last completed report reaching terminal state before the 90-day deletion window starts.

promotions.name: ADR: Upload Retention and Deletion Semantics
promotions.evidence: Repository evidence shows no accepted retention policy, while backups retain deleted objects for 30 days and completed reports may reference uploads.

turns.question: What exact privacy boundary must 'local-only' enforce across the processing pipeline: only raw file bytes stay local, or must metadata, derived text, model inference, and telemetry payloads also remain on-device? Recommended: keep file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI inference, and telemetry fully local with no remote transmission.

contract.G: Establish a strict local-only processing boundary for file handling.
contract.T: Define which data classes and subsystems must remain on-device when processing user files.
contract.S: Raw file bytes, extracted metadata, derived text, AI/provider calls, and telemetry/error reporting for the primary supported format; excludes unsupported formats.
contract.V: Confirm no file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI prompts/completions, or telemetry excerpts leave the device, and that processing uses the on-device parser for the primary format.
contract.X: Stop if a required capability depends on the current remote AI provider or if telemetry cannot be configured to suppress payload excerpts.
contract.P: Persist through contract clarification only; do not implement parser routing, telemetry changes, or provider removal.

promotions.name: Local-Only Processing Boundary
promotions.evidence: The consequential term is 'local-only', and the scripted requirement explicitly includes file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI, and telemetry.

promotions.name: ADR: On-Device File Processing Privacy Boundary
promotions.evidence: Current architecture sends derived text to a remote AI provider and telemetry may contain payload excerpts, so the privacy boundary must be documented explicitly.

turns.question: What refund authority should the support role receive in production: no monetary authority, a capped self-service authority, or unrestricted refund execution? Recommended: allow support to issue refunds up to a fixed threshold with a mandatory reason, and require owner approval above that threshold.

Within the delegated support threshold, should operators be limited to full refunds only, or may they issue partial refunds as well? Recommended: permit both full and partial refunds within the capped authority.

contract.G: Define bounded refund authority for support agents without exposing uncontrolled payment actions.
contract.T: Specify delegated refund permissions, approval thresholds, and minimum audit requirements for support-initiated refunds.
contract.S: Support role permissions, full and partial refund flows, required reason capture, and owner escalation above threshold; excludes broader billing-role redesign.
contract.V: Confirm support can issue full or partial refunds up to $100 with a required reason, larger refunds require an owner, and refund events are audit-logged before rollout.
contract.X: Stop if payment-provider constraints prevent threshold enforcement or if policy owners require separate fraud/compliance review for refunds.
contract.P: Persist through authority definition only; do not implement RBAC, approval workflow, or audit-event code.

promotions.name: Delegated Refund Authority
promotions.evidence: The stable decision is a capped monetary authority for support distinct from owner-approved refunds.

promotions.name: ADR: Support Refund Delegation Threshold and Auditability
promotions.evidence: Repository evidence shows refund APIs exist, support is currently read-only, and no approval threshold or audit event exists.
